title: Guidelines for AI procurement - GOV.UK
date: unknown (page shows © Crown copyright 2020; exact publication date not shown)
claim: UK government guidance says buyers should form a multidisciplinary team, conduct data discovery and iterative impact assessment before market engagement, frame output-based requirements around the problem, and require lifecycle governance, knowledge transfer, training, and ongoing support.
limitations: Official guidance rather than an outcome study; it targets UK public procurement and is likely older than 18 months if the 2020 copyright date reflects publication.

title: Enterprise AI Strategy & Readiness Consulting | Coditas
claim: Coditas describes a strategy/readiness engagement that reviews current AI activity and constraints, scores readiness, prioritizes use cases, builds a 12–18 month execution roadmap, and defines a first-pilot pack with scope, metrics, data, delivery model, and handover plan; it says artifacts can be taken forward by internal teams, existing partners, or Coditas.
limitations: Supplier marketing and self-description; no independently verified client evidence or outcomes, and the page date is unknown.

title: AI Strategy: A Roadmap From Readiness to Implementation | Forvis Mazars US
date: March 2026 (URL gives month; exact publication day not shown)
claim: Forvis Mazars distinguishes strategy (what/why, readiness, operating model, governance) from implementation (delivery roadmap, workflow integration, change, measurement, improvement), then proposes governance, outcomes, readiness-matched use cases, people/process/technology/data foundations, ownership and decision rights, and implementation in waves.
limitations: Consulting thought leadership and not independent causal evidence; cited survey figures are reported by the source and should be cross-checked against the underlying reports.

title: Enterprise AI transformation: how leading organizations are redesigning operations around AI
claim: Dataiku argues that pilots stall when people, systems, and governance are disconnected; it recommends one accountable pilot owner, outcome-linked metrics rather than model accuracy alone, an MLOps baseline, governance from day one, and sequencing two or three high-impact workflows that share infrastructure.
limitations: Vendor-authored promotional guide; survey, customer, time-to-delivery, and benefit claims are not independently validated here.

title: What UAE enterprises with AI plans must do – put data first
claim: A UAE-focused Gulf News commentary by HPE’s UAE/Africa managing director says enterprises can have abundant but fragmented, unstructured, siloed data; it recommends a single source of truth, data governance, security, cleansing, and an AI-ready storage foundation before implementation.
limitations: Expert commentary, not a representative study or procurement record; older than 18 months as of 2026-09-14 and should be read as a UAE-relevant perspective rather than prevalence evidence.

title: AI³ Delivery Partners Project - Find a Tender
claim: The UK Department for Business and Trade describes an AI³ model with an AI Lab for rapid exploration, an AI Factory for developing and operationalising experiments into production-ready tools, and AI Operations for maintenance and scaling; it procured specialist teams and individuals to join internal teams across those stages.
limitations: The notice establishes one buyer’s delivery model and resourcing need, not general prevalence; it does not list the specific use cases or detailed success measures.

title: Procuring AI - AI Knowledge Hub
date: unknown (page is marked draft; examples refer to 2025)
claim: The UK AI Knowledge Hub draft says AI procurement still requires competition, value-for-money, data protection, security, and documented decisions; it presents a competitive-flexible route using short working prototypes and cites a planning-decision procurement targeting a reduction from 8+ weeks to 4 weeks before full deployment.
limitations: The page explicitly says it is a draft, not comprehensive, and not legal advice; the planning example is an illustrative government procurement route, not evidence that the target was achieved.
